scope: FDIC deposit-insurance rules, Federal Reserve monetary policy benchmarks, U.S. Treasury daily par yield curve benchmarks, and official national rate benchmarks anchored to Account Open Date 2026-10-22.

coverage_limits.rule: All single accounts owned by the same person at the same insured bank charter (CERT) — including principal plus accrued interest — are added together and insured up to $250,000.
Each co-owner's shares of every joint account at the same insured bank are added together and insured up to $250,000 per co-owner ($500,000 total for two equal co-owners).
All self-directed retirement deposit accounts owned by the same person at the same bank charter are added together and insured up to $250,000.

coverage_limits.category: Trust account (revocable POD / irrevocable, up to 5 beneficiaries)
coverage_limits.rule: Unified FDIC trust rule: # of grantors/owners x # of unique eligible beneficiaries x $250,000, capped at $1,250,000 per grantor per bank charter across 5+ beneficiaries ($2,500,000 for 2 co-grantors with 5+ beneficiaries).
Each participant's non-contingent interest is insured up to $250,000 per bank charter; for contingent interests coverage is $250,000 for the plan itself.

covered_products: Cashier's checks, money orders, and prepaid cards meeting FDIC pass-through rules
not_covered_products: Mutual funds (including money market mutual funds)
Safe deposit boxes or their contents
U.S. Treasury bills, bonds or notes (backed by full faith and credit of the U.S. Government, not FDIC)

key_rules.text: FDIC insurance is automatic for deposit accounts at an FDIC-insured bank; depositors do not apply for it.
Coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per ownership category, per separately chartered FDIC-insured bank (CERT) — principal plus unpaid accrued interest count toward the $250,000 ceiling.

Divisions or online sub-brands sharing the same FDIC Certificate (such as Capital One & merged Discover Bank under CERT 4297, or BMO & Alto by BMO under CERT 16571) share a single $250,000 limit per ownership category.
Depositing exact $250,000.00 principal into a single-owner account leaves Year-1 accrued interest ($8,750–$10,625 at 3.50%–4.25% APY) uninsured unless capped at $250,000 / (1 + APY) or swept monthly.

national_rates.publication: FDIC National Rates and Rate Caps - October 2026 (published third Monday, October 19, 2026)

treasury_yields_pct.note: Treasury yields published inside the FDIC National Rates table (as of 2026-10-19); latest daily U.S. Treasury par curve (2026-10-21) is also provided in daily_treasury_par_curve below.

fomc_policy.action: Raised target federal funds range by +25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%; reserve balances rate set to 3.90% effective 2026-09-18.

rate_cap_note.text: The FDIC national rate cap applies to less-than-well-capitalized institutions and is not a market rate for consumers. For savings it is 4.63% as of 2026-10-19 (national average 0.38% + 75 bps or 120% of Treasury).
